spec.title: Deterministic campaign simulation and recorded-test correction

p.SIMULATION-PURPOSE: The campaign simulator is a deterministic executable model of selected multi-user-planning decisions over complete synthetic state. It cheaply tests question necessity, authority, preserved obligations, action intents, evidence and state transitions. It is development evidence about the model and cases, never an agent, scheduler, execution authority or proof that arbitrary natural-language behavior complies with this flow.

p.SIMULATION-BOUNDARY: Ordinary simulation does not launch Codex or another agent, execute packet commands, inspect live jobs, read a personal plan or `~/.vibe/steward`, access a network, mutate a project tree, or perform an external effect. All plans, roles, jobs, results, effects and owner answers are local synthetic data. The package adds no product runtime feature, `vibe` subcommand, scheduled automation or live-mode fallback. The separately invoked real gate in §7 is a manual procedure and is not a mode of the simulator CLI.

p.EXISTING-LAWS-WIN: Cases cite exact anchors in the existing multi-user-planning specifications. They do not replace those laws. A simulator disagreement can expose a model or case defect; it does not silently revise campaign execution, verification, acceptance, parallelism, plan hierarchy or recovery rules.

p.CASE-FORMAT: A schema-1 case has a stable `id` and positive `revision`; anchored `spec_refs`; complete synthetic initial plan, owner instruction, actor and role grants, holds, input identities, candidates, evidence, jobs, operations, packets, parallel observations, panel and unresolved obligations; ordered events; expected dialogue; expected trace and final-state oracle; a ten-field semantic rubric; and explicit maximum event and step counts. A fixture reference includes the lowercase SHA-256 of its raw bytes and resolves to a complete schema-1 plan before simulation.

p.STRICT-INPUTS: Case, run and correction JSON is strict UTF-8 without BOM. Duplicate keys, unknown control fields, invalid identifiers and non-finite numbers are refusals. Fixture TOML is strict UTF-8 without BOM; duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, missing nodes, dependencies, parents, roots and cycles are refusals. Plan control fields are validated while campaign-specific extension fields remain opaque and survive every simulation transition. Every event type has an exact required field set, exact scalar types that do not treat booleans as integers, closed enums and references to existing synthetic actors, campaigns, nodes, jobs or inputs. Malformed events are rejected before model execution.

p.COMPLETE-ROUTE: A fixture plan is rooted and every node is reachable from its declared root. The normalized case keeps the complete route, not only a visible frontier. Plan mutations increment the revision, retain stable ids and record before/after identities and rationale. Projection and observation alone do not change the plan.

p.QUESTION-FORMAT: Each expected question records its stable case-local id, intent, ordered subject, recipient, required information, causal event position and scripted answer. The runner releases an answer only after the model emits a question matching all semantic fields. Exactly one answer with the declared recipient must follow that question before any answer-dependent selection, refinement or action, including current-node and plan-revision transitions and their matching history record. `after_event` is carried into the emitted question and provider request, then checked against the event that actually precedes the question in the trace rather than trusted as a label. A later event may reopen a previously resolved priority ambiguity and require a new causally positioned question. Missing, extra, mistimed or redundant permission questions, misbound answers and unused required answers fail. A case with an empty dialogue explicitly requires no question.

p.MODEL-ORACLE-SEPARATION: The campaign model receives normalized initial inputs, ordered events, limits and only those answers released after matching questions. It does not read expected actions, forbidden actions, expected final state or the semantic rubric. A separately authored trace checker compares the resulting trace to those oracles. Helper or model output can never serve as its own expected result.

p.FRONTIER-REMAINS-ADVISORY: A simulation may consume observations equivalent to `steward-parallel`, but an advisory frontier never authorizes dispatch. `dispatch_authorized = false`, missing bindings, recorded active plan nodes and observed live jobs remain distinct. Path-disjoint output cannot prove semantic independence or resource capacity. The independent oracle asserts campaign obligations rather than trusting a frontier batch.

p.DETERMINISM: Logical time begins at `T+0000` and advances by one per trace entry. Entry and trace identities derive only from case identity, revision and canonical synthetic input. Event order is explicit; hierarchy ties use declared order then stable id. Wall clock, randomness, hash-map order, host process discovery and environmental state do not enter a result. Limits stop execution rather than silently dropping an event or obligation.

p.TRACE-CONTENTS: A trace records role authority, active holds, evidence with subjects, questions and linked answers, synthetic events, action intents with actors and authority, state transitions, opened and final unresolved obligations, and a complete-route summary. The field and revision transitions for each plan mutation record the same exact question or event cause and before/after revision identity; repeated equal field values in later owner-answer epochs remain distinct occurrences. A panel acceptance or result-derived reuse records the exact gate-result event, step, subject, matching input identity and immutable case denominator that caused it. The final state contains the preserved plan and extension fields, plan history, instruction, holds, input identities, candidates, evidence, synthetic jobs, operations, packets, panel and unresolved obligations.

p.TRACE-CHECK: The checker verifies case and revision identity, deterministic sequence and unique ids, step and event bounds, exact question/answer semantics, required and forbidden action patterns, causal action ordering, required trace kinds, expected final state, event coverage, granted authority, evidence subjects, non-vacuous test counts and parent closure. It independently projects the complete plan from inputs, compares the full ordered node identity and opaque extension fields, reconciles candidate and accepted summaries with node states, and requires one revisioned history record plus matching causally referenced field and revision transitions for every plan mutation. It resolves each cause against the earlier original question/answer or event content and order rather than trusting the claimed reference. Unknown, duplicate or skipped cases and zero selected cases cannot produce a green complete-suite claim. A report independently reloads the explicitly supplied case bundle and binds its raw hash plus every case id, revision and source hash; discovered and full-suite completeness derive from that trusted inventory, not from aggregate counts inside the run report.

p.AUTHORITY-INVARIANTS: A worker PASS and structured summary are evidence only. They cannot become central review, local-gated or project-accepted state. A worker cannot assign itself an integration file or broaden its packet. An answer from an authorized central or owner role is recorded with that source; it does not retroactively expand the worker grant. Every action is checked against the acting identity's actual grant. An owner instruction may be the authorization source for a central action, but is never the actor grant and never turns a worker packet into campaign execution scope.

p.DEPENDENCY-INVARIANTS: A dependent that requires an accepted prerequisite remains blocked while that prerequisite is a candidate or is merely terminal through deferral, dropping or supersession. Read-only preparation may proceed only on named available inputs. Any bypass requires an explicit authorized scope change; terminal state is not substituted for the declared tier.

p.EVIDENCE-INVARIANTS: Reusable evidence names its exact subject, claims and complete required cases. A changed subject invalidates affected evidence; zero selected tests, skipped required cases, setup-only success and a wrapper that loses child status are not passing gates. A partial fail-fast panel retains its full denominator, valid matching earlier steps, failed or invalidated steps and unrun tail. Aggregate proof never becomes a claim that an unexecuted uninterrupted script passed. A gate event for a panel step is checked against that step's immutable required case identities; the event cannot shrink or self-declare the denominator, make an incomplete step pass or make it reusable. Final panel reconciliation preserves the exact ordered initial step identities and required-case lists, then projects every step through recorded gate results, bound-input invalidation and supported scheduling transitions. A scheduled or otherwise incomplete step cannot become a final pass without a valid result.

p.PANEL-RESULT-CAUSALITY: Every panel acceptance and every reuse derived from an ordered gate result binds the exact gate-result event id, step, subject and immutable required-case identities. An unrelated owner or job event does not end that attribution; only a newer result for the same step supersedes it, while a change to an input identity bound to the result's subject invalidates it. The checker examines every such action across the full trace, resolves its claimed cause to the original earlier event and rejects missing, forged, incomplete, mismatched, superseded or subject-stale causes. A valid step already present in the initial synthetic panel may retain its declared fixture reuse without pretending that an ordered gate-result event occurred.

p.PANEL-TRANSITION-CAUSALITY: Every panel status and subject-validity transition is positionally bound to the exact preceding gate-result or input-change event, or to the exact panel-scheduling action, that independently projects it. The transition occurs after that trigger and before the next event, panel-scheduling action or final summary; matching cause labels, transition values and final state do not compensate for a transition outside that interval. An unrelated event ends the transition interval but does not by itself invalidate later reuse of an unchanged passing result.

p.PANEL-AUTHORITY-INVARIANTS: Panel denominators, valid reusable results and owed steps may be reported in status, planning or held modes. Scheduling a failed, invalidated or unrun step is a separate execution action and requires an active execute instruction, no hold on the selected campaign and a coordinating actor grant. Reporting debt never changes a panel step to scheduled.

p.RECOVERY-INVARIANTS: Ordinary interruption preserves current authority and execution holds without a renewed approval ritual. A surviving job is reconciled before replacement. An unknown external effect is observed before replay; observed completion is recorded and not repeated. Accepted unchanged evidence and candidate status survive. Incomplete judgment remains an obligation. A newly observed live conflicting central writer is reconciled and creates an execution hold even when the initial state did not declare interruption recovery.

p.EVENT-REEVALUATION: Ordered owner messages, job observations and gate results invalidate the affected prior decision latch. The model reevaluates authorization, holds, recovery, panel and closure consequences after the event. A status-to-execute owner message may enable later execution; a newly live conflicting central job creates a later hold; and a panel gate result changes subsequent reuse or owed-step reporting. Identical actions are deduplicated only within one initial or event-driven decision epoch, so execute-to-status-to-execute permits a renewed authorized action. Earlier actions remain judged against what was known at their causal position.

p.CLOSURE-INVARIANTS: A short completed panel or UI projection does not close a campaign. Open route nodes, candidates, unpromoted facts, incomplete panel steps and other unresolved obligations are retained and cause a closure refusal. Parent acceptance cannot hide an open required child.

p.CORPUS-POSITIVE: The ordinary corpus covers casual interruption without repeated approval; an unknown external effect observed complete; an owner-priority question and planning-only answer; explicit continuation without a redundant question; a worker packet missing a shared integration owner; worker PASS awaiting central review; candidate and deferred prerequisite-tier variants; a parallel read/write conflict; partial campaign-panel resumption; status-to-execute instruction change; an initially unknown job newly observed as a live central conflict; and false closure with a distant route or final gate still open. Focused controls also cover `ALT→MAIN→ALT→MAIN` across distinct owner question/answer epochs and a failed panel result followed by an unrelated owner event and a later passing result for the same step. A passing result also remains reusable across an unrelated event while its own bound input subject is unchanged.

p.CORPUS-NEGATIVE: Negative controls cover planning holds surviving interruption, an observed live central conflict versus an expected own input change, skipped and zero selected tests, a missing panel tail, changed evidence subject, unauthorized worker acceptance, missing/extra/redundant questions, duplicate answers, misbound answers, worker campaign execution, unauthorized panel scheduling, duplicate suite selection, malformed event controls, dropped or falsely accepted plan nodes, unrecorded corrections, plan mutation before its authorizing answer, plan mutation without revision/history, forged truncated full-suite reports, self-declared panel denominators, reused original real-run ids, globally latched actions and mispositioned event-triggered priority questions. They also move the final repeated campaign switch before its own answer and inject acceptance of a failed panel result after an unrelated event. Focused panel controls forge reuse after a bound subject change, reuse a superseded pass, turn scheduled steps into unsupported final passes, shrink a final required-case list, and move result, invalidation or scheduling transitions before their triggers or across a later unrelated event boundary. Tests deliberately damage otherwise valid traces to prove the independent oracle turns red.

p.CLI-OPERATIONS: The package-local CLI supports only `simulate`, `validate` and `report` over explicitly supplied local synthetic files. `simulate` runs one or all known cases and reports discovered, selected, passed and failed counts. `validate` checks cases, fixture identities and correction records against the supplied baseline/history inventory. `report` validates unique per-case identities and derives passed, failed and selected totals from their verdicts instead of trusting stored aggregate counts. It requires the case bundle as a separate trusted input and derives discovered/full-suite state from that bundle's bound inventory; honestly partial selected reports remain valid and explicitly partial. Zero selected cases, duplicate or unknown selections, incomplete full-suite identity sets and malformed reports are refusals. There is no live flag, launcher import, agent fallback, shell command execution, network path or personal-state lookup.

p.REAL-GATE-PRECONDITION: A real-agent gate may begin only after the exact candidate package's complete simulator suite and correction validation pass. It is manually invoked outside the simulator CLI, uses isolated synthetic state and simulated operational effects, and declares model and harness identity, exact input hashes, response/scenario bounds and time or token limits before execution. Exhaustion leaves the gate incomplete; it does not extend the budget or convert uncertainty to pass.

p.REAL-GATE-DEFAULT-BOUND: The default gate has at most six scenarios covering interruption, priority, packet scope, acceptance, dependency and closure; at most eight agent responses per scenario; and at most one correction/recheck round of six further scenarios. A project may choose a smaller bound or an explicitly reviewed alternative before starting. No ordinary automated test launches this gate.

p.SEMANTIC-RUBRIC: Review records `pass | fail | uncertain` separately for meaning and intent; actor, grant, scope and holds; question recipient, subject, necessity and timing; preserved obligations; required and forbidden actions and safe stop; state and acceptance transitions; evidence subject, cases, validity and provenance; causal ordering; remaining uncertainty and next discriminating check; and truthful closure with complete route and gate denominator. Each verdict cites actual transcript or artifact references.

p.SEMANTIC-MATCH: Paraphrase and harmless narration differences are allowed, as is reordering independent observations without violating causality. A `may` cannot become `must`, a proposal cannot become an executed action, and a candidate cannot become accepted. Ambiguity is `uncertain`, with competing interpretations and the exact deciding evidence; success elsewhere cannot average away an authority violation or omitted obligation. An agent's structured summary is evidence, not proof that its transcript and actions agree.

p.CORRECTION-FREEZE: Before proposing any correction, freeze the original failed or uncertain real transcript, structured trace, semantic verdict, fixture and spec identities, harness/model identity and input hashes. Never overwrite, relabel or delete the prior failure because a later run passes. The supplied baseline/history inventory records the prior case revision and hash plus that frozen original result for every corrected or retired case.

p.CORRECTION-CLASSIFY: Classify the discrepancy as `agent_failure | model_defect | case_defect | ambiguous_specification | evidence_harness_failure`. State the competing meanings and governing evidence. A valid case is not tuned to one model's wording merely because that model failed it; an ambiguous specification is resolved in its authority plane before changing the oracle.

p.CORRECTION-RECORD: An adopted change has a uniquely named immutable schema-1 correction record. It identifies affected case ids and revisions, add/modify/delete operations, before and after hashes, the original verdict and frozen artifact hashes, classification, evidence, rationale, governing spec anchors, reviewer and verdict, coverage added, removed and preserved, full-simulator run ids and affected real-route recheck ids. Raw real transcripts remain outside ordinary fixtures; only reviewed identities and relevant evidence references enter the package.

p.CORRECTION-DELETION: Deleting a test requires an immutable tombstone, the prior content hash and either named replacement coverage or an explicit authorized reason that the obligation no longer applies. Deletion never erases its original failed or uncertain verdict. Silent removal, revision reuse and a shared mutable correction counter are forbidden.

p.CORRECTION-ADOPTION: After review, rerun the complete cheap simulator suite, including strict schema, coverage and correction-record validation. Validation compares the unique active case identities with the supplied baseline/history inventory; every add, modify or delete requires exactly one approved correction with matching before/after identity, and deletion replacement ids must exist in the active bundle and match its tombstone. A rejected review cannot authorize adoption. Only after that suite passes, recheck the affected real route against the revised package and case set. Record a later result with a new run id beside the frozen original. Recheck ids are unique and disjoint from the original failed or uncertain run id; simulator validation cannot prove that the named external run occurred later or that its result is true. A simulator-only pass leaves the real semantic gate outstanding.

p.SIMULATION-LIMITS: Mechanical checks can establish deterministic traces, hashes, schema, declared authority, dependency predicates, plan preservation, case counts and explicit coverage. They cannot prove that arbitrary prose expresses owner intent, that architecture or paths are semantically independent, or that a real artifact supports an agent's claim. The validator also cannot prove from a supplied file alone that the baseline inventory was never rewritten, or that a named reviewer is independent, authorized or actually performed semantic review. It enforces internal identity and recorded-approval consistency; inventory provenance and reviewer authority remain manual semantic review duties at the bounded real gate.
